prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Restaurant Dinner Menu (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes.
Merged cells: "Starters" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Mains" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Desserts" spans 4 col × 1 row.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Dish" · longest unbreakable unit 77px · widest one-line content 164px
  col 2: header "Description" · longest unbreakable unit 83px · widest one-line content 558px
  col 3: header "Price" · longest unbreakable unit 37px · widest one-line content 37px
  col 4: header "Allergens" · longest unbreakable unit 70px · widest one-line content 298px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Present a dinner menu that helps diners choose dishes with awareness of ingredients, prices and allergens.","tasks":["Scan dishes by course.","Read descriptions to compare dishes.","Find each dish's price and allergen information."],"relations":["Each dish, description, price and allergen entry belongs to the same row.","Course headings group the dishes that follow them."],"roles":["Dish names are row headers and primary lookup anchors.","Descriptions provide explanatory prose.","Prices are compact values for comparison.","Allergen entries provide dish-specific dietary information.","Starters, Mains and Desserts are full-width group headings."],"keep_whole":["Individual words and ingredient names.","Price values and their currency symbols.","Allergen terms.","Dish names where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Descriptions at natural word boundaries.","Multiword dish names and allergen lists when needed."],"same_scale":["Dish rows should have a consistent hierarchy across courses.","Course headings should share the same full-width treatment.","Prices should occupy a consistent, compact column."],"h_vs_v":"Description prose can absorb several lines, while dish names, prices and allergens benefit from enough width for quick scanning. Allocating more width to descriptions reduces row height; allocating more to allergens or dish names improves those lookup paths but makes descriptions taller."}

d3r3A: column widths [185, 330, 58, 146] px · table 720×467 px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 60, 36, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d3r3B: column widths [175, 325, 58, 161] px · table 720×467 px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 60, 36, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d3r2A: column widths [185, 335, 58, 141] px · table 720×467 px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 60, 36, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
